assessment.nobel_worthiness: A new class of electronic matter whose protected edge and surface states were predicted and then actually measured: the quantum spin Hall state in HgTe wells and later 3D topological insulators seen by photoemission. The discovery opened a field of materials and device physics and it has clear experimental footing, which is what I look for.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the decisive theoretical prediction of the quantum spin Hall state. Molenkamp's group gave the first experimental realization (HgTe, 2007), following the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal, whose authors are not among the credited names. Hasan's 3D topological insulator photoemission work is a further original experiment. Only three can be named, so I leave Hasan out reluctantly and flag the allocation as open.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed independently by many groups in transport and ARPES for over fifteen years. The interpretation is stable and recognition is well timed.
uncertainties: The credited list omits Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang, so the theory-credit set is incomplete.
Choosing between Molenkamp (2D, transport) and Hasan (3D, spectroscopy) for the experimental slot is unresolved; B033 and B029 overlap with this entry.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Flat bands at the magic angle, correlated insulators and superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene opened a tunable platform for strongly correlated physics in a single, clean material. It is a discovery that many experimentalists could not see before. I value that the experiments are direct and reproducible.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted the magic angle (2011). Jarillo-Herrero's group made the original observation of correlated insulators and superconductivity (2018). Andrei's group made earlier STM and transport observations of the flat bands and the twist-angle dependence. Bistritzer is a co-author of the key theory paper, and the prize cannot cover all four, so the theory credit is a real constraint.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced by many groups worldwide and the field is expanding quickly. Some interpretations of the superconducting mechanism are still unsettled, but the experimental discovery is secure.
uncertainties: Which of Bistritzer and MacDonald is credited, and how much weight Andrei's earlier STM work carries, are unresolved.
The pairing mechanism is still debated, which may make the recognition seem early to some members.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantized conductance in steps of 2e^2/h in a point contact is a textbook original experiment: simple, unambiguous and it made mesoscopic quantum transport visible. Not a beautiful instrument, but exactly the original observation, and it underpins quantum dots and later devices.
assessment.attribution: The Delft/Philips group (van Wees and coworkers) and the Cambridge group (Wharam, Pepper and coworkers) published within weeks of each other in 1988, so the original credit is shared across two groups. The three credited names cover both groups, but other co-authors such as Thornton, Ford and Beenakker are outside the list.
assessment.maturity: Very mature. It has been reproduced and extended for over thirty-five years, so if anything the question is why recognition is late, and whether priority issues have gone stale.
uncertainties: Whether the committee can fairly limit this to three people from two groups.
Historical priority between the two near-simultaneous papers should be checked in the original record.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Metal halide perovskites turned into efficient photovoltaic absorbers in about fifteen years, with efficiencies rivalling silicon. This matters for humanity through energy, and it is materials physics I know well, though much of the real progress is chemistry and device engineering.
assessment.attribution: Miyasaka reported the first perovskite-sensitized solar cell (2009) in the original experiment. Park made the first solid-state cell with durable efficiency (2012 with Gratzel's group), and Snaith reported the meso-superstructured cell and thin-film efficiencies (2012). Gratzel and others made contributions that are outside the list, and the physics-versus-chemistry boundary is a concern.
assessment.maturity: Efficiency results are confirmed by many labs, but long-term stability and manufacturing remain open, so it may be early for a prize about lasting impact.
uncertainties: Stability and commercial viability are unproven.
The Nobel physics mandate may sit uneasily with a chemistry-led device story.
Credit beyond the three named people is contested.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks with the magic-wavelength idea reached a fractional uncertainty near 1e-18 and are positioned to redefine the second and enable tests of fundamental physics and geodesy. An instrument that really opens a door to measurement.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed and demonstrated the magic-wavelength lattice concept (2001-2003), and Ye's group brought the clocks to the highest precision and stability. Both strands are clear and the two-person set is coherent, though other clock developers (Hall and Hansch in 2005 were recognised for combs, and Ludlow, Lemke and others) are not named.
assessment.maturity: Comparisons between independent laboratories confirm the performance, and the redefinition of the second is under discussion. The timing is reasonable.
uncertainties: Neighbouring prizes in this area (2005, 2012) may be felt to make this a second-round recognition.
Contributions from other clock groups are not captured by the two names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Atomic-resolution AFM with CO-functionalized tips, imaging the chemical structure of single molecules and bond order, is an instrument breakthrough of the sort I find compelling. It lets people see what they could not see before.
assessment.attribution: Giessibl introduced the qPlus tuning-fork sensor, and Gross and Meyer at IBM Zurich demonstrated the functionalized-tip imaging of molecules in 2009. The three-person grouping is natural, but I need to be sure that the original AFM concept (Binnig, Quate, Gerber) and later refinements are properly separated; this is a refinement of a known method rather than a new first observation.
assessment.maturity: Widely adopted and reproduced across many labs. Interpretation of the images is stable, though the discovery may be viewed as an advance on an existing technique.
uncertainties: Whether a technique refinement qualifies as a discovery or invention in the committee's sense.
Priority relative to other groups using tuning-fork sensors and CO tips.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Large room-temperature tunnel magnetoresistance in magnetic tunnel junctions, and especially the giant effect in crystalline MgO barriers, is the basis of modern hard-drive read heads and MRAM. The impact on technology is large and the physics (spin-dependent tunnelling) is clear.
assessment.attribution: Moodera (and Miyazaki) reported room-temperature TMR in 1995. Yuasa and Parkin, in 2004 and with independent confirmations, showed giant TMR with MgO. Miyazaki is also an original discoverer and the three-name limit forces an uncomfortable choice. The 2007 prize for GMR is a related but different discovery.
assessment.maturity: Mature and in production for many years. Timeliness is fine, even late.
uncertainties: Which of Moodera and Miyazaki is credited for the 1995 result.
Overlap with the prize already given for GMR may weigh against it.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: IceCube opened neutrino astronomy by detecting a diffuse flux of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos and later a source (TXS 0506+056) and the Galactic plane. The detector is a major instrument that opens a new window. I weigh it highly on that basis.
assessment.attribution: The credited name is only Halzen, who conceived and led IceCube, but a prize for such an instrument raises the collaboration problem: the original idea, the AMANDA precursor, the construction and the analysis involved many people not listed here. I am not sure a fair configuration can be reached from this credit.
assessment.maturity: Detections have multiple-sigma significance and are supported by independent follow-up, but the astrophysical sources are only partly identified and the interpretation is still developing.
uncertainties: Single-name credit may not represent the people who did the original work.
Previous neutrino-related prizes (2002, 2015) may affect how the committee sees this.
